properties.decision: UNDECIDED, and it is Anthony's call. The schema declares BOTH `SUPERSEDES` and `OBSOLETES` for the same relationship — one node retiring another on the record — and NEITHER is read by any computation. The choice is which one is the real vocabulary, and then making it mean something. Option A: keep `OBSOLETES` (the one the code and the retire-from-design skill already use) and delete `SUPERSEDES` from the schema and from docs/three-axes.md. Option B: keep `SUPERSEDES` (the one the schema's own doc comment describes as "target retired on the record") and migrate the code. Option C: both survive with a stated distinction — but nobody has yet said what that distinction would be, and two words for one relationship is how a vocabulary rots.
properties.name: OPEN — retirement is two edge types and neither is consulted: which one survives?
properties.rationale:
FOUND BY THE SCHEMA SWEEP, 2026-07-28, and it is the `req:supporting-is-not-conflict` shape at edge level rather than property level.

WHAT WAS MEASURED. `SUPERSEDES` has ZERO references in the entire Rust source: nothing creates it, nothing reads it. It is nonetheless documented in `nodes.rs` ("source supersedes target — target retired on the record") and named in `docs/three-axes.md` as part of what covers the time axis. `OBSOLETES` is the one actually in use — `collapse_decision` draws it when a chosen alternative retires the losers, and the retire-from-design skill instructs users to draw it for a capability or component with a successor. But `OBSOLETES` has NO READER either: grep across the whole core crate finds the constant, the one create site, and a doc comment. No rollup, detector or report consults it.

WHAT THAT MEANS TODAY, stated exactly rather than dramatised: retiring something marks it and changes nothing downstream. A retired capability still counts in every rollup, still raises its gaps, still appears in delivery arithmetic. It is currently LATENT — reflow2's own design contains zero instances of either edge, so the retire path has never been exercised on this project — but the skill is actively telling users to draw an edge that has no effect, which is worse than an edge nobody knows about.

WHY IT IS NOT JUST HOUSEKEEPING. `req:intent-preserved` ("the past is never overwritten") is the requirement retirement serves, and the retire-from-design skill exists precisely to force the question "was this ever true?" — history retired on the record versus a mistake deleted. That whole discipline currently terminates in an edge nothing reads. Whichever edge survives, the deciding question is the same: what SHOULD consult it — delivery roll-up, the gap detectors, `graph_report`'s counts — and does a retired node stop counting, or count separately?

DELIBERATELY LEFT `proposed`: this is a vocabulary choice with migration consequences for anyone who already drew either edge, and `dec:certainty-derived` forbids recording it as settled on the user's behalf.
